body:
EPISODE PACKAGE
====

EPISODE TITLE: THE BLURRY ONION
SUBJECT / TOPIC: INTEGRATED SCIENCE / The Cell
GRADE: Grade 8 JSS
AGE RATING: 10+ (student-safe)
DURATION: 8 minutes
VISUAL STYLE: naturalistic live-action look with clear prop inserts (or 2D/3D cartoon adaptation of the same blocking)

LEARNING TIE-IN: Obtain a clear view and labelled drawing of plant cells

LOGLINE: A student cannot see onion cells until she learns microscope parts and magnification, then finally draws a clear plant cell.

WORLD & CAST

• Setting / era: INT. school science lab
• FAITH: Grade 8 learner, frustrated then concerned. Costume: school sweater.
• MR. OTIENO: lab teacher, calm coach. Costume: lab coat.
• BRIAN: lab partner who rushes focusing. Costume: school shirt.

SCREENPLAY

SCENE 1 — EXT./INT. OPENING LOCATION — DAY

ACTION: FAITH enters the world of the story with a clear goal: Obtain a clear view and labelled drawing of plant cells. Camera follows hands and faces, not a chalkboard.

FAITH
If I can just get this right today, everything else will fall into place.

MR. OTIENO
Then stop guessing. Show me what you think is happening.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Wide establishing → medium two-shot. Ambient authentic location SFX. Soft hopeful underscore.

SCENE 2 — SAME / NEARBY — DAY

ACTION: Obstacle appears. Stakes rise. Props related to the science idea are handled as real objects, not lecture aids.

FAITH
It looks simple. Watch me do it the usual way.

BRIAN
If you are wrong, we lose time — and maybe more than time.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Close-ups on props and worried eyes. Tension riser.

FAITH
If we ignore the detail, we will repeat the same mistake under pressure.

MR. OTIENO
Then name the detail out loud while you do the action — teaching by doing, not by speech notes.

SCENE 3 — CONFRONTATION — DAY

ACTION: WRONG WAY: Brian cranks the high power first and squashes the slide. The problem worsens. Meaning stays in action and argument — characters never read notes aloud.

FAITH
See? I did what everyone does.

MR. OTIENO
And it got worse. That means your idea about it is incomplete.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Handheld urgency. Cut to the failed result.

SCENE 4 — DISCOVERY — DAY/NIGHT

ACTION: A clue appears through action — a label, a measurement, a safer method, a remembered rule spoken as dialogue while doing.

MR. OTIENO
Look at what actually changed. Name it properly.

FAITH
Wait… if that is true, then I was measuring the wrong thing.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Insert shots of evidence. Music shifts from tension to curiosity.

FAITH
If we ignore the detail, we will repeat the same mistake under pressure.

MR. OTIENO
Then name the detail out loud while you do the action — teaching by doing, not by speech notes.

SCENE 5 — SECOND ATTEMPT — DAY

ACTION: RIGHT WAY: Faith starts low power, calculates magnification, focuses carefully. Characters perform the corrected action step by step.

FAITH
This time we follow the rule, not the rumour.

BRIAN
I can see the difference already.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Cleaner framed shots; success micro-beats.

SCENE 6 — COMPLICATION — DAY

ACTION: A new obstacle or time pressure forces them to apply the idea again, proving it was not luck.

BRIAN
We are not done. Another problem just arrived.

MR. OTIENO
Same science. Fresh situation. Go.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Parallel cut or ticking clock motif without graphic peril.

FAITH
If we ignore the detail, we will repeat the same mistake under pressure.

MR. OTIENO
Then name the detail out loud while you do the action — teaching by doing, not by speech notes.

SCENE 7 — RESOLUTION — DAY

ACTION: Payoff: goal achieved. Characters show the result; still no voice-over lecture.

FAITH
It worked because we used the idea correctly — not because we pushed harder the same wrong way.

MR. OTIENO
Say the reason in your own words before we pack up.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Warm wider shot; relieved faces; result hero insert.

SCENE 8 — BUTTON — DAY

ACTION: Final acted beat tying emotion to the learning without reading notes aloud.

BRIAN
Next time someone guesses, we will ask for the reason.

FAITH
And we will check the evidence first.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Slow push-in; music resolves.

FAITH
If we ignore the detail, we will repeat the same mistake under pressure.

MR. OTIENO
Then name the detail out loud while you do the action — teaching by doing, not by speech notes.

BOOKENDS

• COLD OPEN (max 10s): Quick hook image of the failed first attempt — then cut to title THE BLURRY ONION.
• CLOSING REFLECTION CARD (max 10s): On-screen question — How do you calculate total magnification? Answer must match lesson solutions (Eyepiece × objective).

CAPTIONS

FAITH: If I can just get this right today, everything else will fall into place.
MR. OTIENO: Then stop guessing. Show me what you think is happening.
FAITH: It looks simple. Watch me do it the usual way.
BRIAN: If you are wrong, we lose time — and maybe more than time.
FAITH: See? I did what everyone does.
MR. OTIENO: And it got worse. That means your idea about it is incomplete.
MR. OTIENO: Look at what actually changed. Name it properly.
FAITH: Wait… if that is true, then I was measuring the wrong thing.
FAITH: This time we follow the rule, not the rumour.
BRIAN: I can see the difference already.
BRIAN: We are not done. Another problem just arrived.
MR. OTIENO: Same science. Fresh situation. Go.
FAITH: It worked because we used the idea correctly — not because we pushed harder the same wrong way.
MR. OTIENO: Say the reason in your own words before we pack up.
BRIAN: Next time someone guesses, we will ask for the reason.
FAITH: And we will check the evidence first.

ASSET LIST

• Characters: FAITH, MR. OTIENO, BRIAN
• Costumes: as listed above
• Locations: INT. school science lab
• Props: topic-authentic objects for The Cell
• Key shots: failed attempt insert, evidence insert, successful payoff insert

Study pages available for fidelity: 20
DRAMA NOTE: No voice-over of lesson notes. Meaning travels through action and in-character dialogue.

DISPLAY-CLEAN: PASS | fixes: headings=0 bold=0 tables=0 code=0 formulas=0

sources.subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
sources.excerpt: 2.1 The Cell. Cells make up the structure of living organisms and carry out various biological processes. Organisms such as amoeba are composed of a single cell hence are said to be unicellular.
